parts.title: Part 1 — Booking a community sports course
parts.context: A telephone conversation between a receptionist at Northgate Community Sports Centre and a caller enquiring about an adult evening sports course.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Part 1. You will hear a telephone conversation between a receptionist at a community sports centre and a man who wants to book an adult evening sports course. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 6.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Good morning, Northgate Community Sports Centre, Claire speaking. How can I help you today?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Hi Claire. I saw a flyer at the local supermarket about your autumn adult evening courses, and I'd love to sign up for one before all the spots disappear.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: You've called at a good time—we still have places left in several groups. Let me open the enrolment form and take a few details first. Could I have your full name, please?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Sure, it's Daniel Bramwell.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Right, Daniel... is that Bramhall, with an H-A-L-L at the end?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: People get that mixed up all the time. No, it's Bramwell—that's B-R-A-M-W-E-L-L.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Got it, thank you. And because we offer a council discount for residents within the borough, could you give me your street address?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Yes, I've just moved into number 47 Alder Road, right behind the train station.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Sorry, was that Elder Road, like the tree starting with an E?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Ah, close! It's actually another tree—Alder, spelt A-L-D-E-R. So 47 Alder Road.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Lovely, that definitely qualifies for the resident rate. Now, what's the best phone number to reach you on in case a session ever has to be moved?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Let's use my mobile. It's 07492 618350... wait, sorry, hang on, that's my old work handset. My personal mobile is 07492 618305.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Let me read that back to be safe: 07492 618305. Perfect. Now, which sport caught your eye on the flyer?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Well, I originally wanted to book Thursday squash, because I used to play it a bit back in Melbourne. Do you still have room in that class?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Oh, I'm afraid Thursday squash filled up yesterday afternoon, and there are already four people on the waiting list. We do still have spaces in Tuesday indoor volleyball and Wednesday badminton, if either of those appeals.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Tuesdays are tricky with my work shifts, so Wednesday badminton sounds ideal. Let's go with badminton, please.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Great choice—our coach, Gary, is brilliant. We run two Wednesday groups side by side: complete beginners and improvers. Which level would suit you best?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Hmm, I was thinking about joining the beginners group since I haven't picked up a racket in three years, though I did play fairly regularly at university.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Honestly, if you already know how to serve and rally, the beginners class spends the first three weeks on basic grip and scoring, so you might find it a bit slow. Most people with university experience prefer the improvers session.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Fair point—I'd rather get a proper workout. Put me down for improvers, then.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Will do. Just one quick health question for the coach's safety sheet: do you have any current injuries—anything like knee or ankle problems he should know about?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: My knees and ankles are completely fine now, touch wood. The only thing is a mild shoulder injury from moving furniture last winter—it doesn't stop me playing, I just have to warm up slowly before overhead smashes.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Thanks for mentioning that; I'll pop a brief note on the register for Gary.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Now listen and answer questions 7 to 10.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Could you just confirm the dates and times? The flyer said the autumn term begins on the 7th of October.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Most of our courses do start on the 7th of October, yes, including swimming and table tennis. However, the main sports hall floor is being sanded and re-varnished that week, so badminton actually starts a week later, on the 14th of October.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Oh, I'm glad I checked! I'd have turned up to an empty hall. And is it still 6.45 to 7.45 in the evening?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Last term it was just an hour finishing at 7.45, but players asked for longer matches, so we extended it to ninety minutes. That means we still start at 6.45 pm, and you'll finish at 8.15 pm.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Ninety minutes is way better value. Speaking of which, how much is the eight-week block?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: The standard price for non-residents is 76 pounds, which works out at nine pounds fifty a session. Because you live in the borough, though, the local resident discount brings the total down to 64 pounds for all eight weeks.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: That's really reasonable. Can I pay by card when I arrive on the first night, or should I pay over the phone?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Either is fine, though paying at reception ten minutes before your first class saves us reading card numbers aloud. Just remember to bring proof of address like a utility bill.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: No problem. And what about gear? Do I need to buy my own racket and shuttlecocks, or a pound coin for the changing-room lockers?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: We provide spare rackets and plenty of shuttlecocks free of charge. As for the lockers, we actually took out the old coin-operated ones back in June because people never had cash on them. You'll just need to bring a small padlock of your own to secure your bag.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: A padlock—got it, I've got one at home. Thanks so much for your help, Claire.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: You're very welcome, Daniel. See you on the 14th!

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: That is the end of Part 1. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

groups.instructions: Complete the form below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.explanation: Người gọi tự sửa lại khi lễ tân nghe nhầm và đánh vần từng chữ cái họ của mình là B-R-A-M-W-E-L-L.
questions.evidence: No, it's Bramwell—that's B-R-A-M-W-E-L-L.

distractors.why: Lễ tân đoán nhầm đuôi là H-A-L-L ('Bramhall'), nhưng Daniel lập tức phủ nhận và đánh vần lại.

questions.explanation: Daniel đính chính tên đường không phải Elder mà là Alder, đánh vần A-L-D-E-R.
questions.evidence: It's actually another tree—Alder, spelt A-L-D-E-R. So 47 Alder Road.

distractors.why: Lễ tân hỏi lại xem có phải 'Elder Road' bắt đầu bằng chữ E không, nhưng người gọi sửa lại thành chữ A.

questions.explanation: Daniel đọc nhầm số máy công ty cũ rồi tự sửa lại sang số di động cá nhân là 07492 618305, và lễ tân nhắc lại để xác nhận.
questions.evidence: My personal mobile is 07492 618305.

distractors.why: Đây là số máy công ty cũ (old work handset) mà Daniel đọc nhầm trước khi dừng lại sửa thành đuôi 305.

questions.explanation: Môn squash đã hết chỗ và bóng chuyền thứ Ba trùng ca làm việc, nên Daniel chọn cầu lông (badminton) vào tối thứ Tư.
questions.evidence: Tuesdays are tricky with my work shifts, so Wednesday badminton sounds ideal. Let's go with badminton, please.

distractors.why: Daniel ban đầu định đăng ký squash nhưng lớp tối thứ Năm đã kín chỗ và có 4 người trong danh sách chờ.
Lễ tân gợi ý bóng chuyền thứ Ba, nhưng Daniel từ chối vì kẹt ca làm việc.

questions.explanation: Sau khi lễ tân khuyên lớp người mới sẽ hơi chậm với người từng chơi ở đại học, Daniel đồng ý đăng ký trình độ improvers (nâng cao cơ bản).
questions.evidence: Put me down for improvers, then.

distractors.why: Daniel ban đầu cân nhắc lớp beginners vì 3 năm chưa cầm vợt, nhưng đổi ý sau lời khuyên của lễ tân.

questions.explanation: Daniel xác nhận đầu gối và mắt cá chân đều ổn, chỉ có chấn thương vai nhẹ ('mild shoulder injury') từ mùa đông năm ngoái.
questions.evidence: The only thing is a mild shoulder injury from moving furniture last winter—it doesn't stop me playing, I just have to warm up slowly before overhead smashes.

distractors.why: Lễ tân hỏi thăm về chấn thương đầu gối hoặc mắt cá chân, nhưng Daniel nói cả hai đều hoàn toàn ổn.
Được lễ tân nhắc đến như ví dụ nhưng Daniel phủ nhận mình có vấn đề ở mắt cá chân.

parts.title: Part 2 — Tour of a new community library
parts.context: A head librarian welcoming visitors and describing the services and ground-floor layout of the newly renovated Ashbrook Community Library.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Part 2. You will hear a head librarian giving a welcome talk to visitors at the newly renovated Ashbrook Community Library. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Good afternoon everyone, and welcome to the grand reopening of Ashbrook Community Library! My name's Martin, and I'm the head librarian here. Before I walk you through our new ground-floor layout, I'd like to run through a few membership perks and practical updates.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: First, a lot of people have asked what is actually free once you hold a standard library card. Now, printing documents still costs ten pence a page—we tried to scrap it, honestly, but ink budgets wouldn't stretch, though scanning to email is free. On the digital side, though, every card holder gets unlimited free access to borrowing audiobooks through our mobile app, with no late fines because files return themselves automatically.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: What about our upstairs meeting rooms? Local charities and community clubs can use them free of charge, whereas commercial or business bookings carry a small hourly fee to cover heating and cleaning. One brand-new thing that doesn't cost a penny for anyone, however, is attending the weekly digital skills drop-in every Wednesday morning, where volunteers help with everything from online banking to photo backups. Oh, and regarding book holds: standard reservations are free, though fast-track copies of newly released bestselling novels do have a one-pound charge.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: You probably noticed we opened three weeks later than the date printed on our summer banners. Rumours went round that our new shelving arrived in the wrong dimensions, which gave us a laugh because the shelves actually turned up two days early! And the solar panels on the roof sailed through their safety inspection first time. What really held us up was when the builders pulled up the old carpet and uncovered water damage beneath the floorboards from a slow-leaking heating pipe, so the whole sub-floor had to be dried out and replaced.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Now, onto our autumn opening hours. We heard loud and clear from commuters that closing at half past five made it hard to drop by after work. We haven't changed our weekday morning opening—we still unlock the doors at nine o'clock—and Sundays remain afternoon-only from one till four. The big shift is that instead of staying open until eight o'clock on Thursdays only, we're now open late on both Tuesday and Thursday evenings until eight pm.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 15 to 20.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Now listen and answer questions 15 to 20.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Right, if you look down at the ground-floor plan in your welcome folder, you'll see Maple Street running along the bottom and the Main Entrance right in the centre of the south wall. Just inside is our Welcome Desk, and straight ahead runs the Central Walkway leading all the way north to the Garden Patio Door, which opens out onto Mill Pond Garden.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Let's start with our youngest visitors. In the old building, the Children's Story Corner sat immediately to the left of the Main Entrance facing Maple Street—where room A is now—but bus noise from the street kept interrupting storytime. So room A has become our public cloakroom and accessible toilets, and we've moved the Children's Story Corner all the way up to the far north-west corner, looking right out onto Mill Pond Garden, with big beanbags and low picture-book bins.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Next, I know everyone's excited about our new Community Café. Several residents assumed we'd tuck it right next to the Garden Patio Door at the north end, which would have been lovely, except the kitchen plumbing and extraction vents had to connect to the street mains. So as you come through the Main Entrance, turn immediately right, go past the Self-Check Kiosks, and you'll find the Community Café occupying the whole south-east corner facing Maple Street.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Heading back towards the west side now, if you walk past the cloakroom in the bottom-left corner and head north along the corridor with the Main Bookstacks on your right-hand side, you'll reach a glass-walled studio directly opposite those bookstacks. That's our new Digital Media Lab, kitted out with podcast microphones, photo scanners, and editing stations.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: For anyone needing total silence to revise or work from home, we've installed six soundproof Quiet Study Pods. Originally the architects drew them halfway up the east wall beside the Stairs and Lift, which sounded convenient until we realised footsteps and lift chimes would drive students mad. Instead, we tucked the Quiet Study Pods into the far north-east corner of the floor, overlooking Mill Pond Garden, so you get natural light and total peace.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Walk west along the north wall towards the centre and you'll come to two medium-sized rooms flanking the Garden Patio Door. Don't mix them up! The room on the right-hand, east side of the patio door is strictly staff storage and book sorting, so please don't wander in there. The one directly opposite it, on the left side of the Garden Patio Door between the walkway and the Children's Story Corner, is our Local History Archive, housing old Ashbrook maps and newspapers.

script.speaker: Librarian
script.text: Finally, one of our proudest additions is the Tool and Seed Lending Shelf—yes, you can borrow hedge trimmers, wallpaper steamers, and heirloom vegetable seeds! We briefly trialled a small display right near the entrance, but carrying heavy toolboxes across the lobby wasn't safe. Now it sits halfway up the east wall, directly across the corridor from the Stairs and Lift and right between the Quiet Study Pods and the Café, making it super easy to wheel bulky items out. Now, let's grab a coffee and take a look around!

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: That is the end of Part 2. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

groups.title: Free services for library card holders
groups.instructions: Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO services are currently free for all library card holders?

options.text: Printing documents up to twenty pages
Borrowing audiobooks through the mobile app
Booking a private meeting room for business
Attending the weekly digital skills drop-in
Reserving newly released bestselling novels

questions.explanation: Thủ thư khẳng định mọi chủ thẻ đều được mượn sách nói miễn phí không giới hạn qua ứng dụng di động ('unlimited free access to borrowing audiobooks through our mobile app' = B).
questions.evidence: On the digital side, though, every card holder gets unlimited free access to borrowing audiobooks through our mobile app, with no late fines because files return themselves automatically.

distractors.why: In tài liệu vẫn tốn 10 xu mỗi trang ('ten pence a page'); chỉ có scan gửi email là miễn phí.
Phòng họp chỉ miễn phí cho tổ chức từ thiện và câu lạc bộ cộng đồng; đặt cho mục đích kinh doanh (business bookings) vẫn có phí theo giờ.
Đặt giữ sách thông thường miễn phí, nhưng bản đặt nhanh của tiểu thuyết bán chạy mới phát hành (newly released bestselling novels) tốn 1 bảng.

questions.explanation: Buổi hướng dẫn kỹ năng số hằng tuần ('weekly digital skills drop-in') hoàn toàn miễn phí cho tất cả mọi người ('doesn't cost a penny for anyone' = D).
questions.evidence: One brand-new thing that doesn't cost a penny for anyone, however, is attending the weekly digital skills drop-in every Wednesday morning, where volunteers help with everything from online banking to photo backups.

groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.prompt: Why was the library's reopening delayed by three weeks?

options.text: The new shelving arrived in the wrong dimensions.
Water damage was found beneath the old floor.
The roof solar panels failed a safety inspection.

questions.explanation: Nguyên nhân thực sự gây chậm trễ là thợ xây phát hiện hư hại do nước thấm dưới ván sàn cũ từ một ống sưởi rò rỉ ('water damage beneath the floorboards' = paraphrase của 'beneath the old floor').
questions.evidence: What really held us up was when the builders pulled up the old carpet and uncovered water damage beneath the floorboards from a slow-leaking heating pipe, so the whole sub-floor had to be dried out and replaced.

distractors.why: Đây chỉ là tin đồn sai; thực tế giá sách mới đến sớm hơn hai ngày.
Tấm pin mặt trời trên mái đã vượt qua kiểm tra an toàn ngay lần đầu ('sailed through their safety inspection first time').

questions.prompt: What is the main change to the library's opening hours this autumn?

options.text: It now opens earlier on weekday mornings.
It has started opening all day on Sundays.
It stays open late on two evenings instead of one.

questions.explanation: Thay đổi lớn nhất là thư viện nay mở cửa muộn đến 8 giờ tối vào cả tối thứ Ba và thứ Năm thay vì chỉ tối thứ Năm như trước ('two evenings instead of one').
questions.evidence: The big shift is that instead of staying open until eight o'clock on Thursdays only, we're now open late on both Tuesday and Thursday evenings until eight pm.

distractors.why: Giờ mở cửa sáng các ngày trong tuần không đổi, vẫn là 9 giờ sáng.
Chủ nhật vẫn chỉ mở buổi chiều từ 1 giờ đến 4 giờ ('afternoon-only'), không mở cả ngày.

questions.evidence: So room A has become our public cloakroom and accessible toilets, and we've moved the Children's Story Corner all the way up to the far north-west corner, looking right out onto Mill Pond Garden, with big beanbags and low picture-book bins.

distractors.why: A là vị trí cũ của góc thiếu nhi nhưng bị ồn bởi xe buýt trên Maple Street nên giờ đã chuyển thành phòng gửi đồ và nhà vệ sinh.

distractors.why: Nhiều cư dân tưởng quán cà phê sẽ ở sát cửa vườn Garden Patio Door, nhưng hệ thống ống nước buộc phải nối ra mặt đường chính.
Tương tự, cạnh cửa vườn ở phía Bắc không có đường ống nước phù hợp cho bếp quán cà phê.

questions.explanation: Đi qua phòng A (góc Tây Nam) hướng lên phía Bắc, bên phải là Main Bookstacks, thì phòng đối diện trực tiếp với Main Bookstacks bên tường Tây là B.
questions.evidence: Heading back towards the west side now, if you walk past the cloakroom in the bottom-left corner and head north along the corridor with the Main Bookstacks on your right-hand side, you'll reach a glass-walled studio directly opposite those bookstacks. That's our new Digital Media Lab, kitted out with podcast microphones, photo scanners, and editing stations.

distractors.why: A là phòng gửi đồ mà bạn đi ngang qua trước khi tới vị trí đối diện giá sách chính.
C nằm xa hơn ở góc Tây Bắc và là Children's Story Corner.

questions.explanation: Khu học yên tĩnh được đặt ở góc Đông Bắc xa nhất ('far north-east corner'), nhìn ra Mill Pond Garden — tương ứng vị trí F.
questions.evidence: Instead, we tucked the Quiet Study Pods into the far north-east corner of the floor, overlooking Mill Pond Garden, so you get natural light and total peace.

distractors.why: Ban đầu kiến trúc sư định đặt khu này giữa tường Đông cạnh thang máy/cầu thang (G), nhưng đã đổi vì sợ tiếng bước chân và chuông thang máy.

questions.explanation: Phòng Lưu trữ Lịch sử Địa phương nằm bên trái cửa Garden Patio Door, giữa lối đi trung tâm và Children's Story Corner (C) — chính là D.
questions.evidence: The one directly opposite it, on the left side of the Garden Patio Door between the walkway and the Children's Story Corner, is our Local History Archive, housing old Ashbrook maps and newspapers.

distractors.why: E nằm bên phải (phía Đông) cửa Garden Patio Door, nhưng người nói cảnh báo rõ đây là kho nội bộ của nhân viên ('strictly staff storage').

questions.explanation: Kệ cho mượn dụng cụ & hạt giống nằm giữa tường Đông, đối diện trực tiếp với Stairs & Lift và nằm giữa Quiet Study Pods (F) với Café (H) — chính là G.
questions.evidence: Now it sits halfway up the east wall, directly across the corridor from the Stairs and Lift and right between the Quiet Study Pods and the Café, making it super easy to wheel bulky items out.

distractors.why: Kệ từng được thử nghiệm gần lối vào chính, nhưng việc bê hộp dụng cụ nặng qua sảnh không an toàn nên đã dời sang G.

parts.title: Part 3 — Workplace first-aid course assignment
parts.context: Two workplace first-aid trainees, Priya and Sam, discussing their course assignment with their trainer, Helen.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Part 3. You will hear two trainees, Priya and Sam, talking to their trainer, Helen, about their workplace first-aid course assignment for a catering warehouse. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Right, come in both of you, take a seat. I've read your draft audit and emergency handbook for the catering warehouse—really solid fieldwork. Sam, you inspected the existing first-aid kits first, didn't you? What caught you off guard?

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Honestly, Helen, I went in expecting locked cupboards, because someone from another branch told me managers lock kits up to stop staff taking plasters home. Actually every wall box was unlocked and easy to reach, and they even had loads of burn gels right by the hot-drinks station. What genuinely shocked me was checking the dates—nearly half of the sterile dressings had expired, some back in 2021!

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Yeah, nobody had been assigned to audit stock monthly. Then I looked at the emergency contact poster pinned next to the loading bay. Sam thought maybe the print was too tiny for workers wearing safety goggles, though under the LED strip lights it's actually readable enough, and the local hospital address is still accurate. The real mess is that it mixes twenty non-urgent numbers—like the vending machine repair line and payroll—right alongside the ambulance and poison-control numbers.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Oh, that's a classic hazard when someone's panicking—you definitely need to strip that back. Now, turning to your draft incident report form, I have to say your wording is refreshingly clear—none of the heavy medical jargon that confuses warehouse drivers, and you've stayed within staff privacy rules on personal details. My one big concern is that once an injury is logged, there's nowhere at the bottom to note what follow-up actions were taken later, like whether a faulty pallet truck was fixed.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Ah, good catch—without that, the same accident just repeats itself. Before we present the handbook to the warehouse manager on Friday, Sam and I were debating a few tweaks.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: I was keen on translating the whole booklet into three languages straight away, since several packers speak Polish or Portuguese.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Brilliant long-term idea, Sam, though you'll never get accurate safety translations done properly before Friday—save that as a phase-two recommendation.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: True. I also wondered if we should trim the chemical eye-wash section to save pages, since it's three pages long.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Wait—they store concentrated industrial degreasers in aisle four, Priya. Cutting eye-wash steps could be risky. What about adding colour-coded tabs down the edge for different types of injury—burns, cuts, chemical splashes—so anyone can flip straight there?

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Yes! That solves the speed issue without dropping vital detail. Let's definitely put colour-coded tabs in before Friday.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Now let's go section by section through the updates you're planning before you submit. First up, the defibrillator maintenance log.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: I wrote down that the battery lasts five years and the adhesive pads last two, based on an old manual I found online. Priya pointed out that this warehouse has the newer compact model, so I'm going to phone the equipment supplier tomorrow to verify the exact replacement intervals.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Sensible move—never guess with defibrillator specs. What about the choking response guide? Did you notice any duplicate checklists in there?

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: I already stripped out the duplicate checklists last night, Helen. The bigger issue with the choking guide is that it's just dense paragraphs of text, and nobody reads paragraphs when a colleague can't breathe. We're going to drop in a clean step-by-step diagram showing back blows and abdominal thrusts.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Much better. Next, I noticed your fire-assembly and triage map is tucked away on page eighteen.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Yeah, looking back, hiding the evacuation map in the appendix makes zero sense. We've decided to shift it right to the very front of the handbook, on the inside front cover, so it's the first thing staff see.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Great call. Now, on the allergic reaction protocol—the medical steps for auto-injectors look accurate, though I spotted a snag in the footnotes.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Oh, let me guess—the 2016 Health and Safety Executive references! I pulled those from an old template and forgot the regulations were updated last year. I'll swap out those outdated legal references tonight.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Spot on. And how about the solo-worker accident procedure? The warehouse only has two people on site during the overnight cold-store restock, doesn't it?

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Exactly, and neither of us has ever worked an overnight shift, so our draft is mostly guesswork about how their check-in radios work. Rather than guessing, we've booked twenty minutes to interview a night-shift supervisor tomorrow morning and rewrite that part from real experience.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: That'll give your assignment real weight. Finally, the new-starter induction summary—were you thinking of asking one of the senior first-aiders to proofread it?

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Well, since you're assessing the whole draft yourself, we don't really need a senior colleague to proofread it. What worried us is that new hires just skim a one-page leaflet and bin it. So we're going to build in a short practical quiz—just five quick scenario questions at the end—so supervisors can check they've actually absorbed the basics.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Love that idea. Send me the updated file by Thursday evening and you'll be in great shape for Friday.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: That is the end of Part 3. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

parts.title: Part 4 — Urban beekeeping
parts.context: A talk by an environmental researcher on the growth, benefits, and ecological challenges of keeping honeybees in cities.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Part 4. You will hear an environmental researcher giving a talk about urban beekeeping. First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Good evening, everyone. Tonight I want to look at a trend that has reshaped city skylines quietly over the last fifteen years: urban beekeeping. If you climb onto a rooftop in London, Paris, Melbourne, or Chicago today, there's a fair chance you'll spot painted wooden hives buzzing away above the traffic.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Now, when people imagine city hives, they often picture primary schools first, because of educational projects. In reality, strict child-safety liability rules mean schools host only a tiny fraction of hives. Across major cities, rooftop apiaries are far more commonly installed on the flat roofs of hotels, corporate offices, and hospitals—often maintained by specialist contractors who harvest honey for the building's own kitchens.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Why have cities turned out to be surprisingly welcoming for honeybees? Well, we all hear about chemical pesticides harming rural colonies, and that is certainly a major factor. Yet even aside from spraying, modern countryside farmland is often dominated by a single crop, such as vast fields of canola or wheat that bloom for just three weeks and then leave a nutritional desert. Urban bees, by contrast, enjoy a continuous menu of diverse flowering plants from early spring through late autumn.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: This variety shows up directly in the jar. While rural bees rely heavily on field margins and wild hedges, city honey often has an unusually complex flavour because urban bees gather nectar from public parks, apartment balconies, and ornamental trees lining residential avenues—species like lime, horse chestnut, and cherry blossom.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Temperature plays a role as well. Concrete and brick absorb heat during the day and release it slowly after sunset, creating what climatologists call the urban heat-island effect. Researchers initially wondered whether mild winters would cut winter mortality dramatically, though the picture there is mixed. What is much clearer is that because cities stay warmer overnight, the foraging season starts earlier and finishes later, boosting average yields per hive well above nearby rural averages.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: So far, urban beekeeping sounds like an unqualified win for nature. However, ecologists have begun raising serious flags about overcrowding. Many residents assume traffic fumes and air pollution must be the biggest threat to rooftop colonies, yet lab tests rarely find worrying contaminant levels in city honey. Instead, a sudden surge in hobbyist hives across central districts has created intense competition for a finite supply of urban pollen and nectar.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: And honeybees are not the ones losing that battle. A single managed hive can house fifty thousand workers capable of stripping a city park of pollen within hours. While migratory insects like painted lady butterflies pass through briefly, recent surveys in Paris and Montreal show that high honeybee density places severe strain on native species—particularly solitary bumblebees and mason bees that cannot fly far to find alternative food.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: There is also a health risk when enthusiasm outpaces training. Neighbours living near rooftop hives usually worry most about sudden swarms settling in their gardens during May. Swarms are dramatic, yes, but rarely aggressive. Far more damaging is when inexperienced keepers fail to check colonies regularly for parasitic Varroa mites, allowing disease to spread rapidly from one unmanaged roof to surrounding apiaries.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: So what does responsible city beekeeping look like? First, before ordering a colony online, anyone interested should check local height and boundary rules and register with a regional association. Only a handful of city councils operate official hive registries, whereas regional beekeeping associations provide mentors, swarm-collection networks, and local disease alerts.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Second, urban keepers must supply clean drinking water right beside their hives so thirsty bees don't crowd neighbours' swimming pools or birdbaths. Avoid filling a tray with sand, which quickly turns to sour mud; instead, placing a shallow dish of water filled with pebbles gives bees dry landing spots and stops them from drowning while they drink.

script.speaker: Speaker
script.text: Finally, it's worth remembering that honeybees are domesticated livestock, not an endangered wild species. If you want to help urban biodiversity without years of hive training, ecologists now advise skipping the hive altogether. Clipped evergreen shrubs look tidy, sure, yet offer almost zero nectar. Instead, city residents can make a much broader impact by planting pollinator-friendly meadows—even tiny balcony or roadside strips of native wildflowers that nourish hundreds of insect species at once. Thank you very much for listening.

script.speaker: Narrator
script.text: That is the end of Part 4. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

questions.prompt: Hive locations: Commonly installed on the flat roofs of hotels, offices, and {{blank}}.

questions.explanation: Mùa tìm mật kéo dài giúp nâng cao sản lượng trung bình mỗi tổ ('boosting average yields' = paraphrase của 'increasing average yields').
questions.evidence: What is much clearer is that because cities stay warmer overnight, the foraging season starts earlier and finishes later, boosting average yields per hive well above nearby rural averages.

distractors.why: Tỷ lệ chết mùa đông ('winter mortality') được nhắc tới ở câu trước nhưng diễn giả nói kết quả nghiên cứu chưa rõ ràng.

questions.evidence: Instead, a sudden surge in hobbyist hives across central districts has created intense competition for a finite supply of urban pollen and nectar.

distractors.why: Nhiều cư dân tưởng ô nhiễm không khí ('air pollution') là mối đe dọa lớn nhất, nhưng kiểm nghiệm ít khi thấy chất độc đáng lo trong mật ong thành phố.

questions.prompt: High honeybee density puts pressure on {{blank}} species such as solitary bumblebees.
questions.explanation: Mật độ ong mật cao gây áp lực nặng nề lên các loài bản địa ('native species') như ong nghệ sống đơn độc.
questions.evidence: While migratory insects like painted lady butterflies pass through briefly, recent surveys in Paris and Montreal show that high honeybee density places severe strain on native species—particularly solitary bumblebees and mason bees that cannot fly far to find alternative food.

distractors.why: Các loài côn trùng di cư ('migratory insects') như bướm chỉ bay ngang qua trong thời gian ngắn nên không chịu áp lực tương tự.

questions.prompt: Poor mite monitoring by inexperienced keepers allows {{blank}} to spread to nearby roofs.
questions.explanation: Người nuôi thiếu kinh nghiệm không kiểm tra bọ ve ký sinh khiến dịch bệnh ('disease') lan nhanh sang các tổ ong lân cận.
questions.evidence: Far more damaging is when inexperienced keepers fail to check colonies regularly for parasitic Varroa mites, allowing disease to spread rapidly from one unmanaged roof to surrounding apiaries.

distractors.why: Hàng xóm thường sợ đàn ong chia đàn ('swarms'), nhưng diễn giả nói chúng hiếm khi hung dữ và không gây hại bằng dịch bệnh.

questions.prompt: Responsible practice: Check local rules and register with a regional {{blank}}.
questions.explanation: Người muốn nuôi ong cần kiểm tra quy định địa phương và đăng ký với một hiệp hội nuôi ong khu vực ('register with a regional association').
questions.evidence: First, before ordering a colony online, anyone interested should check local height and boundary rules and register with a regional association.

distractors.why: Chỉ rất ít hội đồng thành phố ('city councils') có hệ thống đăng ký chính thức; hiệp hội khu vực mới là nơi nên đăng ký.

questions.prompt: Provide a shallow water dish filled with {{blank}} so bees do not drown.
questions.explanation: Đặt đĩa nước nông có rải đá cuội ('filled with pebbles') giúp ong có chỗ đậu khô ráo và tránh bị chết đuối khi uống nước.
questions.evidence: Avoid filling a tray with sand, which quickly turns to sour mud; instead, placing a shallow dish of water filled with pebbles gives bees dry landing spots and stops them from drowning while they drink.

distractors.why: Diễn giả khuyên tránh dùng cát ('Avoid filling a tray with sand') vì cát nhanh chóng biến thành bùn.

questions.prompt: Residents without training should plant pollinator-friendly {{blank}} instead of keeping hives.
questions.explanation: Các nhà sinh thái khuyên cư dân thành phố nên trồng các thảm hoa đồng cỏ thân thiện với loài thụ phấn ('pollinator-friendly meadows') thay vì tự nuôi ong.
questions.evidence: Instead, city residents can make a much broader impact by planting pollinator-friendly meadows—even tiny balcony or roadside strips of native wildflowers that nourish hundreds of insect species at once.

distractors.why: Cây bụi thường xanh cắt tỉa gọn ('Clipped evergreen shrubs') trông đẹp mắt nhưng hầu như không có mật hoa cho côn trùng.
